papers.title: A note on two problems in connexion with graphs
papers.technique: Greedy relaxation: repeatedly extract the unvisited vertex with minimum tentative distance, relax its outgoing edges. With adjacency matrix and linear scan for minimum, O(n^2).
papers.notes: The foundational SSSP algorithm for non-negative weights. Correctness relies on the fact that with non-negative edges, a vertex's shortest-path distance is finalized once extracted from the priority queue. 26,000+ citations.

papers.title: Fibonacci heaps and their uses in improved network optimization algorithms
papers.authors: Michael L. Fredman, Robert Endre Tarjan
papers.venue: Journal of the ACM (JACM); originally FOCS 1984
papers.technique: Fibonacci heaps: a priority queue with O(1) amortized insert, decrease-key, and merge; O(log n) amortized delete-min. Plugged into Dijkstra's algorithm gives O(m + n log n).
papers.notes: This bound was the best known for SSSP on general directed graphs with real non-negative weights for nearly 40 years (1984-2025). The O(m + n log n) bound matches the sorting lower bound for comparison-based models. 3,181 citations.

papers.title: Faster algorithms for the shortest path problem
papers.authors: Ravindra K. Ahuja, Kurt Mehlhorn, James B. Orlin, Robert E. Tarjan
papers.result: O(m + n sqrt(log C)) SSSP for integer weights in [0, C]
papers.technique: Multi-level bucket structures and radix heaps. Uses the structure of integer keys to avoid comparison-based sorting bottleneck. Exploits the monotonicity of Dijkstra's distance labels.
papers.notes: One of the first significant improvements over Dijkstra+Fibonacci for integer-weighted graphs. 576 citations.

papers.title: Undirected single-source shortest paths with positive integer weights in linear time
papers.venue: Journal of the ACM (JACM); originally FOCS 1997
papers.result: O(m + n) = O(m) SSSP for undirected graphs with integer weights
papers.technique: Component hierarchy (component tree): decomposes the graph into a hierarchy of components based on edge weight thresholds, using word-RAM operations (atomic heaps) to navigate the hierarchy in linear time. Avoids sorting by exploiting that vertices in the same component can be visited in any order.
papers.notes: The first and only linear-time SSSP algorithm without restrictive assumptions on input class. A landmark result showing that SSSP is easier than sorting for undirected integer-weighted graphs. 460 citations.

papers.title: Improved Shortest Paths on the Word RAM
papers.result: O(m + n log w) SSSP for directed graphs with integer weights in [0, 2^w - 1]
papers.technique: Generalizes Thorup's component tree approach from undirected to directed graphs. Also provides a simpler deterministic linear-time construction of the component tree for undirected networks.
papers.notes: Best deterministic linear-space bound for sparse directed networks with integer weights unless w is superpolynomial in log n. As application: APSP in O(nm + n^2 log log n) time.

papers.title: Integer priority queues with decrease key in constant time and the single source shortest paths problem
papers.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences (JCSS); originally STOC 2003
papers.result: O(m + n log log n) SSSP for directed graphs with integer weights; O(m + n log log C) variant
papers.technique: Integer priority queue supporting find-min, insert, decrease-key in O(1) amortized time, and delete in O(log log n) time. Uses exponential search trees and Fibonacci heaps. Plugged into Dijkstra's algorithm.
papers.notes: The best known bound for directed SSSP with integer weights. Improves upon Hagerup's O(m + n log w) for typical word sizes. 180 citations.

papers.title: A Shortest Path Algorithm for Real-Weighted Undirected Graphs
papers.venue: SIAM Journal on Computing, Vol. 34(6), pp. 1398-1431
papers.result: O(m * alpha(m,n) + min{n log n, n log log r}) SSSP for undirected graphs with real weights, where alpha is inverse-Ackermann and r is max/min weight ratio
papers.technique: Hierarchy-based algorithm inspired by Thorup's component tree, adapted for real edge lengths. Uses a preprocessing phase to create a linear-size structure. The hierarchy identifies groups of vertices that can safely be visited in any order.
papers.notes: Optimal in the comparison-addition model for undirected graphs (up to inverse-Ackermann factors). Proposed Omega(m + min{n log n, n log log r}) lower bound for hierarchy-based algorithms. 87 citations. DOI: 10.1137/S0097539702419650.

papers.title: Universal Optimality of Dijkstra Via Beyond-Worst-Case Heaps
papers.authors: Bernhard Haeupler, Richard Hladik, Vaclav Rozhon, Robert E. Tarjan, Jakub Tetek
papers.result: Dijkstra's algorithm is universally optimal for SSSP in both running time and number of comparisons when the output must include the sorted order of vertices by distance
papers.technique: Beyond-worst-case analysis using a novel heap data structure. Shows that for any instance, Dijkstra with an appropriate heap is optimal up to constant factors among all algorithms that produce the vertex ordering by distance. The key insight: if you must output sorted order, you cannot beat Dijkstra.
papers.notes: Critical complementary result to the Duan et al. breakthrough: Dijkstra IS optimal if you require the sorted ordering, but the sorting barrier CAN be broken if you only need distances. 42 citations.

papers.title: A Randomized Algorithm for Single-Source Shortest Path on Undirected Real-Weighted Graphs
papers.authors: Ran Duan, Jiayi Mao, Xinkai Shu, Longhui Yin
papers.result: O(m sqrt(log n * log log n)) randomized SSSP for undirected graphs with real non-negative weights
papers.technique: Randomized ball-growing with carefully chosen centers. Selects random pivot vertices, grows shortest-path balls until pivots are reached, then processes vertices within each ball without full sorting. Avoids the n log n sorting bottleneck for sparse undirected graphs.
papers.notes: First algorithm to break the O(m + n log n) Dijkstra/Fibonacci barrier for real-weighted SSSP on sparse undirected graphs. Subsequently derandomized by Yan (2025). 11 citations.

papers.title: Breaking the Sorting Barrier for Directed Single-Source Shortest Paths
papers.authors: Ran Duan, Jiayi Mao, Xiao Mao, Xinkai Shu, Longhui Yin
papers.result: O(m log^{2/3} n) deterministic SSSP for directed graphs with real non-negative weights
papers.technique: Bounded Multi-Source Shortest Path (BMSSP) framework combined with recursive frontier reduction. Merges ideas from Dijkstra (greedy relaxation) and Bellman-Ford (running it for a few steps to scout ahead). Uses a divide-and-conquer procedure to reduce the frontier set size, breaking the sorting barrier. Dynamic pivot selection and batch-processing data structures.
papers.notes: The first algorithm to break the O(m + n log n) barrier for DIRECTED graphs. Won Best Paper at STOC 2025. Led by Ran Duan's team at Tsinghua IIIS. Demonstrates that Dijkstra's algorithm is NOT optimal for SSSP (when only distances are needed, not sorted order). 18 citations.

papers.title: A Faster Directed Single-Source Shortest Path Algorithm
papers.authors: Ran Duan, Xiao Mao, Xinkai Shu, Longhui Yin
papers.result: O(m sqrt(log n) + sqrt(m * n * log n * log log n)) deterministic SSSP for directed graphs, which is O(m sqrt(log n * log log n)) for sparse graphs
papers.technique: Improves upon the BMSSP framework of Duan et al. 2025. Key new insight: constructs a spanning forest connecting the frontier vertices rather than explicitly mapping each vertex to a source (which incurred a costly Bellman-Ford bottleneck). This avoids the previous O(m log^{2/3} n) bottleneck.
papers.notes: Matches the undirected bound of Duan et al. 2023 (up to derandomization) for directed graphs. The current state-of-the-art for SSSP on directed graphs with real non-negative weights.

papers.title: Lossless Derandomization for Undirected Single-Source Shortest Paths and Approximate Distance Oracles
papers.result: Deterministic O(m sqrt(log n * log log n)) SSSP for undirected graphs with real non-negative weights
papers.technique: Derandomizes the Duan-Mao-Shu-Yin 2023 randomized algorithm. Exploits the fact that ball sizes can be adaptively chosen by the algorithm rather than fixed by input. Provides a simple deterministic algorithm achieving optimal ball size Theta(n/r) on average, avoiding the O(log n) overhead of folklore set-cover-based derandomization.
papers.notes: Also derandomizes the Thorup-Zwick approximate distance oracle without loss in time/space complexity.

papers.title: Bidirectional Dijkstra's Algorithm is Instance-Optimal
papers.authors: Bernhard Haeupler, Richard Hladik, Vaclav Rozhon, Robert E. Tarjan, Jakub Tetek
papers.result: Bidirectional Dijkstra is instance-optimal for point-to-point shortest path (s-t shortest path)
papers.technique: Extends the universal optimality framework from the single-source setting to the point-to-point (s-t) setting. Shows that bidirectional Dijkstra with appropriate heap is optimal for every input instance.
papers.notes: Companion result to the FOCS 2024 universal optimality paper. 4 citations.

papers.title: Simple Universally Optimal Dijkstra
papers.authors: Ivor van der Hoog, Eva Rotenberg, Daniel Rutschmann
papers.result: Simplified proof that Dijkstra is universally optimal, with a simpler heap construction
papers.technique: Provides a simpler universally optimal implementation of Dijkstra's algorithm. Achieves the same universal optimality guarantee as Haeupler et al. 2024 but with a more accessible proof and simpler data structure.
papers.notes: Simplifies the Haeupler et al. 2024 result. 1 citation.

papers.title: Implementation and Brief Experimental Analysis of the Duan et al. (2025) Algorithm for Single-Source Shortest Paths
papers.authors: Lucas Castro, Thailsson Clementino, Rosiane de Freitas
papers.result: Experimental evaluation: Dijkstra remains 3-4x faster in practice; crossover estimated at >10^67 vertices
papers.technique: First faithful deterministic implementation of the Duan et al. 2025 BMSSP algorithm (in C++). Implements worst-case, degree-normalized, and expected-time variants. Tests on sparse random graphs, grids, and US road networks up to 10M vertices.
papers.notes: Demonstrates that while theoretically faster, the Duan et al. algorithm has very large constant factors. Degree normalization hurts in practice; expected-time variant sometimes helps.

papers.title: A Simple Shortest Path Algorithm with Linear Average Time
papers.result: O(m + n log C) worst-case; linear average-case for uniformly distributed weights
papers.technique: Multi-level bucket data structure with caliber heuristic. For positive uniformly distributed lengths, achieves linear average-case time.
papers.notes: Practical algorithm with excellent empirical performance on real-world instances. Engineering perspective on shortest path computation.

papers.title: Single-source shortest-paths on arbitrary directed graphs in linear average-case time
papers.result: O(m + n) average-case SSSP for directed graphs with random edge weights
papers.technique: Analysis of average-case behavior of bucket-based SSSP algorithms on directed graphs with random weights.
papers.notes: Demonstrates linear average-case time for SSSP on arbitrary directed graphs. 82 citations.

papers.title: Negative-Weight Single-Source Shortest Paths in Near-linear Time
papers.authors: Aaron Bernstein, Danupon Nanongkai, Christian Wulff-Nilsen
papers.result: O(m log^8(n) log W) SSSP with negative integer weights
papers.technique: Near-linear time algorithm for SSSP with negative weights, a major breakthrough. Uses price functions, low-diameter decomposition, and scaling techniques.
papers.notes: While this handles negative weights (outside strict scope), it is a landmark result that reshaped the SSSP landscape. Essentially showed SSSP with negative weights is near-linear. 55 citations.

papers.title: Single-Source Shortest Paths (Encyclopedia of Algorithms entry)
papers.venue: Encyclopedia of Algorithms (Springer), ed. M.Y. Kao
papers.result: Survey of SSSP results across all models
papers.technique: Comprehensive survey covering: comparison-addition model (Dijkstra, Fredman-Tarjan, Pettie-Ramachandran), word-RAM model (Thorup, Hagerup), negative weights (Bellman-Ford, Goldberg), and the relationships between SSSP, sorting, and priority queues.

directed_best.bound: O(m sqrt(log n) + sqrt(mn log n log log n))
directed_best.notes: Current state of the art for directed SSSP with real non-negative weights.

undirected_best.bound: O(m sqrt(log n * log log n))
undirected_best.notes: Deterministic via Yan's derandomization of the Duan-Mao-Shu-Yin randomized algorithm.

dijkstra_baseline.notes: Optimal if the sorted order of distances is required (Haeupler et al. 2024). Suboptimal if only distances are needed.

directed_best.notes: Uses integer priority queues with O(1) decrease-key.

key_insights: For 40 years (1984-2025), Dijkstra+Fibonacci heaps at O(m + n log n) was the best known bound for general SSSP with real non-negative weights.
The sorting barrier: it was widely believed SSSP inherently requires sorting, imposing Omega(n log n). Haeupler et al. 2024 showed this is true IF sorted order is required.
Duan et al. 2025 broke the sorting barrier for directed SSSP, showing that computing distances alone (without ordering) can be done in o(m + n log n) on sparse graphs.
The key technique: combining Dijkstra's greedy relaxation with selective Bellman-Ford steps to scout ahead, plus recursive frontier reduction (BMSSP framework).
Integer weights allow much faster algorithms via word-level parallelism (Thorup's linear time for undirected, O(m + n log log n) for directed).
Despite theoretical breakthroughs, Dijkstra remains 3-4x faster in practice; the crossover is estimated at >10^67 vertices.
open_questions: Can directed SSSP be solved in O(m) (linear) time in the comparison-addition model?
Is there a tight lower bound for SSSP in the comparison-addition model (without ordering requirement)?
Can the practical constant factors of the Duan et al. algorithms be improved to make them competitive with Dijkstra?
